p: Oxford Street is Europe's busiest shopping street by many accounts, and on a Saturday afternoon it certainly feels that way. Millions of visitors head here every year for its flagship stores and big department shops, and the crowds can be relentless. Having a games bar in the middle of it all is like finding an oasis in the desert.

Transport-wise, you're spoiled. Oxford Circus, Bond Street, Tottenham Court Road and Marble Arch are all along this one road, and the Elizabeth line stops at Bond Street and Tottenham Court Road. Buses run up and down the street constantly, so getting here and home again is easy.

For the best visit, it pays to plan around the crowds. Weekday evenings are usually a little calmer than weekends, and a mid-afternoon game is a great way to escape the busiest shopping hours. If you're meeting a group, pick a clear meeting point, because it's surprisingly easy to lose people in the crowds outside.

For a breather, Hanover Square and Cavendish Square are small leafy pockets just off the main drag, and Marylebone High Street, a short walk north, has a much more relaxed village feel. The Wallace Collection on Manchester Square is a free museum with an amazing collection of art and armour in a grand townhouse. And Selfridges, at the western end of the street, is worth a nose even if you're not buying anything. Its window displays are a bit of a London tradition in their own right.
